notes: §1985:IV.4.3.8.1 SR3: "uniqueness must then be established through qualification for each user-defined name explicitly referenced, except in the case of redefinition", not every qualifier needed, and "A paragraph-name or section-name appearing in a program may not be referenced from any other program". QualifiedCandidates/UniqueOrReportAmbiguous (COBOL1639) serve every reference; since PB5165 landed, DataBinder.ClauseOperandsTakeImplicitQualifiers (DialectLevel >= 2002) keeps EntryClauseCandidates and RegionClauseCandidates from narrowing to the subject's group at 85. Probed at 85 (classes b, c, d, e): FLD OF REC-A, FLD IN GRP-Y, FLD OF GRP-X OF REC-A, qualified and unqualified-unique condition-names, P OF S / PB IN S1, PB unqualified from its own section, DEPENDING ON CNT OF REC-A, RENAMES X IN R1 THRU Y IN R1, an unqualified REDEFINES of a non-unique X all resolve and run; an unqualified FLD or CNT (also as a subscript), qualifiers out of order, DEPENDING ON CNT, ASCENDING KEY IS FLAG and RENAMES X THRU Y with a second declaration, a non-unique FILE STATUS item, and a contained program's PERFORM of the containing program's paragraph are refused (COBOL1639); at 2002 the three entry clauses compile, as the 2002 exemption allows. PARTIAL: RECORD KEY IS K and ALTERNATE RECORD KEY IS K, with a second K in working-storage, compile and run at 85 (and at 2023): ResolveFiles' local InRecords prefers the candidate inside the file's records instead of counting both. kb/Work PB5566 holds the defect (code read: op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-01.json; rerun op-20261114/records-rs5a/rerun-log.txt). History: until the 1985 re-read 5 (2026-11-14) this row read PARTIAL naming no kb/Work note; the re-read of main dc1f2dcce8 found the defect below still open (or a new one), and kb/Work PB5566 (open) owns it.

next.reason: 1985 requires qualification of every non-unique referenced name 'except in the case of redefinition'. §2023:8.4.2.2.3 SR1 keeps 'uniqueness shall be established through a sequence of qualifiers'. But §2023:8.4.2.2.1 adds exemptions, among them 'The name is a data-name referenced in a data description entry clause whose subject is subordinate to the same group item as that data-name', with implicit qualifiers. So an unqualified non-unique OCCURS DEPENDING ON object that 1985 refused is accepted in 2023 (looser), and the VARYING and type-declaration exemptions cover new features. Special-register qualification is carried by 8.4.2.2.3 SR8 to SR10. The cross-program paragraph/section bar is the uncataloged §2023:8.4.6.1 ('may be referenced only by statements in the source element in which the user-defined word is declared').
